title: Your first script and recording
description: Create a script, save it in your Library, rehearse and record your first video in CueCard for iPhone or iPad.
body:
## Create and save a script

1. Open CueCard. In the Library, choose **Teleprompter** from the mode menu at the top left.
2. Tap **+** at the bottom and type or paste a short script. Try: “Here is one thing I learned today. [pause] Here is how you can try it.”
3. Tap **Save** at the top when you have changes. Tap the title at the bottom to rename it. Return to the Library to find the saved script.

A new script can appear as a draft before you save it. Save the version you want to keep before recording.

## Rehearse, then record

1. Open the script in the teleprompter with the play control. Tap the screen if the reading controls are hidden.
2. Adjust **Scroll Speed** and text size in Settings. Read a few sentences aloud to find a comfortable pace.
3. Tap the camera at the top. Position its small window so you can see your framing and words.
4. Tap the red camera button to record. Tap it again to pause; tap **stop** to finish and save to Photos.
5. Open **Takes** to review the result. The script stays out of the camera footage.

With **Sync with Teleprompter** enabled, playback and recording controls work together. See [recording controls](/help/recording-video/) before a longer take.

## Prefer talking points?

Choose **Cards** in the Library and create one card per idea. Open the deck with **Read Cards** and swipe as you speak. You can record with cards too. Start with a [free cue-card template](/cue-card-templates/).

Before relying on a script for an important talk, [choose a storage folder](/help/storage-and-sharing/) to keep a copy outside the app.

title: Record video with your script or cards
description: Learn CueCard’s camera controls, synchronized playback, pause and stop, and how to find your finished video in Photos.
body:
## Open the camera

Open a saved script in the teleprompter, or open a deck in Cards. Tap the screen if controls have faded, then tap the **camera** at the top. Allow camera and microphone access when asked.

The camera opens in a small window over your reading view. Drag it to a corner, pinch or double-tap to resize it, and tap it to show its controls. Use the camera controls to switch cameras or zoom.

## Record, pause and finish

1. Tap the red camera button to start recording.
2. Tap it again to pause the take while you prepare the next line.
3. Resume when ready. Tap **stop** to finish and save the video to Photos.
4. Open **Takes** above the reading controls or the takes count in your Library to review it.

In Teleprompter mode, **Sync with Teleprompter** links the controls: Play starts recording with the camera open, Pause pauses recording, and the camera’s record/pause actions play or pause the script. Turn this off under **Settings → Camera** if you want separate controls. In Cards, keep turning cards while recording.

## What appears in the video?

Your script and cards stay out of the camera video. **Text Above Camera** changes how text overlaps the camera window on your screen, not the recorded footage. Phone screen recording is different and can capture the visible script.

## If recording does not work

Check CueCard’s camera and microphone permissions in the iPhone or iPad Settings app. Check available device storage and the message shown when a take cannot save. Finish with stop, then look in Photos and [check Takes access](/help/takes/).

To record in another app instead, close CueCard’s camera and use the [floating teleprompter](/help/floating-window/). The floating window does not open while CueCard’s camera is on.

title: Fix or set up the floating teleprompter
description: Keep your script above another app and troubleshoot a missing floating window without losing your saved notes.
body:
## Start the floating window

1. Save your script, then open it in **Teleprompter** mode.
2. Tap the screen to reveal the controls. Tap the Picture in Picture button, labeled **Start Overlay**, or leave CueCard while the teleprompter is open.
3. Open the app you want to record in. Move the script near the camera lens without covering that app’s recording controls.
4. Record a short camera clip and review it before a longer take.

You should see a small script window above the other app. Your camera video does not include this window; a phone screen recording can.

## The window does not appear

- **Close CueCard’s camera first.** The floating window cannot open while the built-in camera is on.
- **Open the reading view.** Leaving the Library or editor is not the same as leaving the teleprompter.
- **Try Start Overlay directly.** If leaving the app does not start Picture in Picture automatically, use the button in the teleprompter. Also check **Settings → General → Picture in Picture** on your device for automatic PiP behavior.
- **Return to CueCard and reopen the reading view.** Save edits before closing anything. There is no need to delete the app to try this.

## The other app interrupts the session

Camera, audio and streaming behavior can vary between apps and versions. Test the specific recording workflow you need. If it does not work reliably, [record in CueCard](/help/recording-video/), finish the take, and upload the saved video to your social app.

For support, include your device, iOS version, CueCard version, the other app’s name, and whether the overlay fails before or after recording begins. [Contact support](/support/).

title: Find, review and organize your Takes
description: Find recorded videos, resolve Photos access issues, and understand how favorites, albums and deletion work in CueCard.
body:
## Find a recording

Videos recorded with a script or deck open are associated with it as **Takes**. CueCard can also associate videos saved to Photos while its teleprompter floats over another recording app.

1. Open the script or deck you used.
2. Tap **Takes** above the reading controls, or tap its takes count in the Library.
3. Tap a video to play it inside CueCard.

Videos live in **Photos**. Takes is a way to review and organize those videos alongside your script, not a second independent video backup.

## Review and keep the strongest take

Add tags and notes below a playing video, such as “clear opening” or “redo the final line.” Tap the heart to favorite it; it becomes a favorite in Photos too. Touch and hold a take, or open it, and choose **Add to Album** to put it in a Photos album.

## A take is missing

First check Photos. Finish an in-app recording with **stop** so it saves. A recording made in another app must be saved to Photos; a draft kept only inside that app is not a Photos video.

Check CueCard’s Photos access in device Settings. Limited access can prevent a video from appearing; allow access to the relevant video or expand access if you want CueCard to find it. Check the original script or deck rather than a different copy.

If Photos no longer has the video, CueCard cannot play it from its own separate copy. If you deleted it, check Photos’ Recently Deleted album.

## Deleting a take

**Deleting a take in CueCard deletes the video from Photos too.** Swipe left on a take, or open it and choose Delete. Keep or export any video you need before deleting it.

title: Set up Follow Me AI (Beta)
description: Make the teleprompter follow your spoken script, check microphone and speech permissions, and return to fixed-speed scrolling.
body:
## Turn on voice-following

Open a script in the teleprompter and tap the **waveform** at the top. Follow Me AI is off each time you open the teleprompter, so activate it for the session you want to use it in.

If the control is hidden by your setting, look for **Follow Me AI** under **Settings → Apple Intelligence**. Availability of controls and settings can vary with your device. Update CueCard if you are using a release from before this beta was added.

Allow **microphone** and **speech recognition** access when asked. Read the words in your script aloud. The reading position follows your speech, and the timer starts with your first words. Tap Pause to stop listening and Play to listen again.

## Requirements and privacy

Follow Me uses on-device speech recognition and requires support for the script’s language on your device. Your voice is processed on the device. It is a beta: recognition may struggle with background speech, unfamiliar names, or words that differ substantially from the script.

Its speech-recognition requirements are separate from the Apple Intelligence model used by [Suggestions AI](/help/ai-suggestions/). Do not assume that availability of one guarantees the other.

## If the script does not follow

- Check microphone and speech-recognition permissions in device Settings.
- Read a complete sentence from the current script in a quiet place.
- If CueCard reports an unsupported language, use fixed-speed scrolling for that script.
- If you skip a large section, drag to the place you want to read or jump to an [anchor](/help/mirror-and-reading-guide/), then continue from there.

## Use a set pace instead

Turn off the waveform mode and set **Scroll Speed** in Settings. Fixed-speed playback does not need speech recognition. Rehearse the mode you intend to use before recording; [compare the two approaches](/blog/voice-following-vs-fixed-speed/).

title: Use Suggestions AI and Help AI (Beta)
description: Review on-device writing suggestions and learn why Apple Intelligence features may be missing or unavailable in CueCard.
body:
## Check availability

Suggestions AI and Help AI need **iOS or iPadOS 26 or later**, a device that supports Apple Intelligence, and Apple Intelligence enabled and ready. They are not available on every device that can run CueCard. Device, language and model availability can affect whether the controls appear.

If CueCard says Apple Intelligence is still getting ready, wait for the device’s model to become available. If it is off, turn it on in device Settings. CueCard’s own feature switches are under **Settings → Apple Intelligence**.

## Review writing suggestions

1. Open a script or deck in the editor.
2. Tap the **sparkles** button at the bottom left.
3. Read each suggestion in context. Tap it to accept or reject it.
4. Tap sparkles again when you are done, then save the edits you want to keep.

Suggestions may include spelling fixes, missing words, rewrites, cues, formatting, paragraph breaks and script anchors. Cards omit anchors and only get cue suggestions where there is room. Your script is reviewed on the device; you choose which edits to apply.

## Ask for help

Open the question-mark help button. On a supported, ready device, **Help AI** lets you ask questions about using CueCard. You can also browse the help topics. Treat beta answers as guidance and check the relevant steps if an answer does not match your screen.

## No AI control?

You can still write, edit, save, record, use cards and browse help without these models. Check that the relevant feature is enabled, and confirm your device’s Apple Intelligence availability. [Follow Me AI](/help/voice-following/) uses speech recognition and has its own requirements.

title: Save scripts, collections and versions
description: Find the current Save controls, organize your Library in collections, and compare or restore earlier script versions.
body:
## Save and find your work

CueCard opens on the **Library**. Choose Teleprompter or Cards from the top-left menu. Tap a script to edit it and return to the Library when finished.

When there are changes, the editor shows **Unsaved** at the bottom and **Save** at the top. Tap Save to keep them. To keep the changes as a separate script, open the editor’s **••• → Save as New**. Tap the title at the bottom to rename it.

A new unsaved script appears as a draft. Save a named version before an important session.

## Organize collections

1. In the Library, tap **+** after the collections or choose **••• → New Collection**.
2. Swipe a script right or touch and hold it, then choose **Add to Collection**.
3. Tap a collection to see its scripts; tap **All** to see every script in the selected mode.

New or imported scripts go into the collection you are viewing. Touch and hold a collection to rename or delete it. Choose **••• → Sort By** to change the order.

## Restore an earlier version

Every save creates a version. Tap the version number at the bottom of the editor to compare changes and restore an earlier save. Once a script has multiple versions, you can also open **••• → Version History**.

If you cannot find a script, check both modes, select All, and search your Library. Version history belongs to the app’s saved note; a shared text file is not a copy of that history.

For copies that remain outside CueCard, [choose a storage folder](/help/storage-and-sharing/) before uninstalling the app.

title: Keep, import and share your scripts
description: Choose a storage folder before removing CueCard, import scripts, and share text or a TextPack with images.
body:
## Keep a copy outside CueCard

Until you choose a storage folder, scripts are kept inside the app and are deleted when you delete it.

1. Save your scripts in the Library.
2. Open **••• → Choose Storage Folder** in the Library. If one is already set, the option is **Change Storage Folder**.
3. Choose a folder you can find again in Files. Choose one in iCloud Drive if you want the files stored there.
4. Check that the expected files are present before removing the app or changing devices.

This keeps the latest saved note files outside CueCard, along with collection information and images. Images and collection information use hidden files in the folder, so preserve the whole folder when moving a backup. Choose that folder again after reinstalling to bring the notes back. It is not a backup of everything in the app: version history stays in CueCard. Videos remain in Photos. Keep a separate shared copy of important scripts, including their images, before deleting the app.

## Import a file

In the Library, choose **••• → Import File** and select your script. CueCard supports text-file import and TextPack packages for scripts with images. Open the imported note to check the text and images before relying on it.

## Share text or images

Touch and hold a script in the Library and choose **Share**. A script without images is shared as text with its cues. A script with images is shared as a **TextPack**, which includes the images. Keep that package together rather than copying only its text.

## Where your data goes

CueCard does not upload scripts to a CueCard account. Choosing a folder in iCloud Drive or another file provider uses that provider’s storage. The chosen folder is a file-based workflow, not a promise that all app state or version history synchronizes between devices.

If files stop appearing, check that the chosen folder is available in Files and that its provider has finished downloading. Save and share an important script before troubleshooting. [Contact support](/support/) if a file cannot be imported; describe the file type without sending private script contents unless needed.

title: Mirror text, move the reading guide and use anchors
description: Set horizontal or vertical text flipping for teleprompter glass, position the reading line and jump between script anchors.
body:
## Mirror for teleprompter glass

1. Open **Settings → Teleprompter**.
2. Turn on **Flip Horizontally** or **Flip Vertically** to suit your glass and screen orientation. Both are off by default.
3. Put the device in the rig and read a short line through the glass. Adjust the flips until the reflected words read correctly.

The floating window uses these text-flip settings too. Check the reflected view rather than judging only the device screen. [See the mirror setup guide](/teleprompter-mirror/).

**Mirror Front Camera** is different: it changes the saved front-camera video. Text flipping changes what you read. One does not configure the other.

## Put the reading line near your eyeline

The pointer beside the script marks the line to read. Drag it up or down to put the reading position where your eyes naturally fall; the script lines up with it. To hide it, turn off **Reading Guide Line** in Settings.

Choose a comfortable text size, then rehearse from your actual speaking position. A very wide line can make your eyes sweep noticeably across the screen.

## Mark places to jump to

In the editor, tap **+ Anchor** above the keyboard or type an anchor such as **[anchor]**. In the teleprompter, use the far-left and far-right buttons to jump to the previous or next anchor.

Place anchors at the opening, demonstration and closing of a long script. Rehearse the jump before filming. Colored cues such as **[pause]** are reminders for you; they do not pause playback automatically.

title: Use cards on the Lock Screen and Apple Watch
description: Set up Lock Screen cards, install the Watch app, keep a deck on your wrist and control teleprompter playback.
body:
## Read cards on your Lock Screen

1. Choose **Cards** in the Library and open or create a deck.
2. Open the deck with **Read Cards**.
3. Turn on **Show on Lock Screen** in Settings, then lock your iPhone.
4. Use **Back** and **Next** on the Lock Screen to move through the deck.

The Lock Screen shows a compact card view, so keep important prompts near the beginning. Images appear as a photo symbol on the Lock Screen and Watch; use text for information you need to read there. If the activity is missing, check that Live Activities are allowed for CueCard in device Settings and reopen the deck.

## Install and connect Apple Watch

Open the **Watch** app on your iPhone. Under **Available Apps**, tap **Install** beside CueCard. The app requires watchOS 10 or later.

Open a script on iPhone to control its teleprompter from the watch: play, pause, go back ten seconds and see the timer. Open a deck on iPhone to read cards on the watch; turning a card on either device moves both.

## Read a deck without your phone

Touch and hold a saved deck in the iPhone Library and choose **Keep on Apple Watch**. Open CueCard on the watch and check the deck is there before leaving the phone behind. This keeps a deck on the watch; remote control of a phone teleprompter still needs the phone.

If the watch returns to the clock too quickly, open the Watch app and choose **General → Return to Clock → CueCard → 1 hour**. If a deck is missing, bring the paired devices together, open both apps and try keeping it on the watch again.

title: Choose camera settings for your next take
description: Set video resolution, frame rate, dynamic range, codec, stabilization and front-camera mirroring in CueCard.
body:
## Choose your recording preferences

Open CueCard’s **Settings → Camera**. Choose the available resolution, frame rate, dynamic range, codec and stabilization options. Turn on **Mirror Front Camera** if you want the recorded front-camera image to match its mirrored preview.

These are preferences, not a guarantee that every camera supports every combination. CueCard records as close to your preferences as the selected camera allows. Switching cameras can change what is available. A change made during recording applies to the **next take**.

## Start with a short test

1. Choose your settings before recording.
2. Open the camera in a script or deck and select the camera you plan to use.
3. Record a short clip with the lighting and movement you expect in the finished video.
4. Stop to save it, then play it in Photos or Takes. Check framing, sound, orientation and the result in the app where you plan to post it.

If a preferred combination is unavailable, choose from the options offered for that camera rather than assuming a particular resolution or frame rate is supported on every device.

## Keep reading and recording comfortable

**Text Above Camera** keeps your words visible over the camera window. Turning it off puts the camera preview on top instead. Neither setting puts the script in the saved video.

**Sync with Teleprompter** links script playback and camera recording in Teleprompter mode. Turn it off if you want to start and pause them independently. [Read the recording steps](/help/recording-video/).

To reverse text for a glass rig, use **Flip Horizontally** or **Flip Vertically** under Teleprompter, not Mirror Front Camera. [Set up mirroring](/help/mirror-and-reading-guide/).
